posts.text:
$PLTR 

Palantir, once again, puts up one of the best quarters that the market has ever seen.

Being able to grow revenues 96% while having 62% adjusted operating income margins is unheard of. There is no other software company that is even close to putting up these types of results.

US commercial revenue officially passed US government revenue for the first time. I remember in 2022, the bear case was centered around the company being too reliant on the USG. If anything, that was the bull case because that gave them the time to figure out how to scale US commercial and now we have a company doing 29% growth QoQ, which would be amazing YoY for most companies as Dr. Karp said, but also scaling that YoY growth at 148% for US commercial. 

It is unprecedented. 

So, why? Why is it happening? 

Well, it seems like Sovereignty is a very, very big deal.

“The Sovereign AI movement is imposing the most dramatic dichotomy between haves and have nots that I have witnessed in 30 years of business. Every institution—government and commercial—is rapidly being forced, voluntarily or not, into one of these two categories,” said Alex Karp.

Having been to multiple AIPCons and Institutional Sovereignty bootcamps this year, I can say that this is very real. When you talk to customers, you realize that they want much, much more than just plugging their enterprise into an LLM. They actually want FDEs, they want the grunt work of figuring out how to build custom workflows, they want the post training and fine tuning of open models...they want outcomes. The reason Palantir is growing this fast and continuing to show so much operating leverage is because they are delivering outcomes. That's why this is working. 

The company is doing this with 1090 customers. Most enterprise software companies at this scale have well over 100K customers. I mean, once again, this is unprecedented. Their net dollar retention scaled to 165%...their rule of 40 is now a new record at 158%...these are numbers that you only get when the company's entire mission is geared towards making sure their partners succeed and as a result, they are being paid for that value and then monetizing that value at the highest efficiency any software company ever has before with these margins. 

Stock is down due to macro, midterms, etc. but the core business is growing faster than anything we have ever seen and doing so in one of the most profitable ways ever. Their adjusted FCF in 90 days is now equal to the revenue they were bringing in early last year. 

An incredible quarter by Palantir, congrats to all shareholders and a deep thank you to the executive team and employees.

Meta is lining up an AI bond deal of at least $20B, split across dollars and euros. Bloomberg reported at about 12:16 PM ET that Citi and Morgan Stanley are holding investor calls today and tomorrow. The plan is five dollar tranches and six euro tranches, which would be Meta's first euro bond, and the deal could grow if demand is strong. There's no price talk yet. That makes Meta the third hyperscaler in high-grade today, after Oracle and Alphabet, and it comes on top of last month's shelf registration and forward stock sale. The things to watch are how much extra spread Meta has to pay, whether its CDS widens, and whether demand holds up after Oracle's slide. (Bloomberg)

Oracle's $10B bond and $10B stock sale still hadn't priced as of 3:30 PM ET. The stock is down about 8.6% at around $126.

Ratings. Fitch kept Oracle at BBB and said it doesn't expect much more capital raising. Moody's affirmed its rating and kept the negative outlook.
Credit. The 6.85% 2066 bonds fell more than 1.2 points, and five-year CDS is still around 296 bp.
Next. Final pricing should be in the next run's update. (Yahoo Finance)

Weekly KAOS - The Bullwhip & The Canary

A small wobble in end demand snaps hardest UPSTREAM where the chips, data centers and power sit, and because that upstream now runs on Debt rather than Equity, Credit is the Canary in the Coalmine.

Welcome to the Weekly KAOS — UrbanKaoboy’s end-of-week roundup covering Macro and Geopolitics, where I try and tease out the most impactful bits of the week.

Themes of the Week

The AI trade finally cracked this week, tech tumbled and bonds rallied into the growth scare, which is the Bullwhip snapping upstream and the Credit Canary singing louder.

Anyone who has studied supply chains knows the Bullwhip Effect, where a modest wiggle in end demand gets amplified as it travels upstream, so that a 5% bump at the retailer can balloon into a 40% swing at the factory. As I posted this week, I am not nearly smart enough to know how the AI/Anthropic story ends, but the Bullwhip Effect really concerns me.

Everyone is frothing over that parabolic ARR and forgetting that Anthropic sits near the FRONT of the Bullwhip, while the truly capital-hungry links, the chips, the servers, the gigawatts, sit far UPSTREAM. That is exactly where a small crack at the handle becomes a violent snap at the tip.

What makes the Bullwhip dangerous rather than merely interesting is how that upstream is now financed. The buildout has shifted from Equity “funny money” to Debt, so the first place a slowdown shows up is not the stock tape but Credit. I laid out the mechanic

quoted.text:
De Raad van State is bijzonder kritisch over de nieuwe box 3-plannen.

Het advies is duidelijk: trek het huidige wetsvoorstel in en kom met een nieuw stelsel dat in 2030 ingaat.

En daarmee worden meteen een paar problemen opgelost!

Het was namelijk al de bedoeling om vanaf 2030 ook goud en bitcoin onder de vermogenswinstbelasting te brengen. 

Als het kabinet het advies van de Raad van State volgt en in 2030 in één keer overstapt op een nieuw stelsel, verdwijnt ook het probleem van de tijdelijke ongelijke behandeling tussen vermogensaanwas- en vermogenswinstbelasting.

Daarmee verdwijnt bovendien een belangrijke aanleiding voor nieuwe rechtszaken.
En dan zijn ook die 252 extra fte die de Belastingdienst tijdelijk nodig zou hebben voor de voorgestelde wijzigingen niet meer nodig. 

Mooi, want het kabinet heeft voor de zoveelste keer beloofd de overheid nu écht kleiner te maken. Overigens waren er voor de nieuwe box 3-plannen al 900 extra fte voorzien.

Dus we moeten niet te snel conclusies trekken. En al helemaal niet stoppen met beleggen vanwege de onzekerheid rond box 3.

Dat neemt niet weg dat een aantal fundamentele problemen gewoon blijft bestaan. Zoals het exorbitant hoge belastingtarief van 36% en het feit dat inflatie niet wordt gecompenseerd. Je betaalt dus ook belasting over rendement dat je koopkracht helemaal niet vergroot.  Daar schreef ik eerder al een artikel over.

De Raad van State heeft bovendien een belangrijk punt: waarom met zoveel haast een ingewikkeld

Positioning in the US dollar is at one of the most extreme levels we’ve seen in years.

The currency is also deeply overvalued and technically stretched.

With rates rolling over and the Fed nearing the end of its hiking cycle, we may be approaching a major turning point.

Meanwhile:

Gold and silver are deeply oversold — a reversal in the dollar could unleash a powerful rally in both metals.
